chunks: Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abi Najran, from Asim ibn Humayd, from Muhammad ibn Qays, from Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him), who said:
Amir al-Mu'minin (peace be upon him) judged regarding an eye of a horse whose eye was blinded, [paying] a quarter of its price on the day its eye was blinded.
ai.seo_question: What is the compensation for blinding a horse's eye in Shia Islamic jurisprudence?
ai.summary: This hadith from *Al-Kafi* illustrates the practical application of *diyah* (blood money) in early Islamic jurisprudence, specifically highlighting the principle that compensation for animal injury is assessed based on the market value at the time of the incident rather than a fixed statutory amount. It reflects the Imam’s role in resolving civil disputes with precision, establishing a precedent for calculating damages in property and livestock cases within Shia legal tradition.

en.hubeali:
Ali Bin Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abu Najran, from Aasim Bin Humeyd, from Muhammad Bin Qays, 
(It has been narrated) from Abu Ja’far<sup>asws</sup> having said:
‘Amir Al-Momineen<sup>asws</sup> judged regarding an eye of a horse which was blinded (by someone), by a quarter of its price on the day its eye was blinded (price when horse had both eyes)’.
